newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo customs tariff bill aims to protect industry.
newsitem.headline: Yugo customs tariff bill aims to protect industry.

text.p: The Yugoslav government drafted a customs tariff bill which it said would be a basic long-term instrument for the protection of domestic goods, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Tuesday.
"In drafting the bill the government took the position that all imported goods are subject to customs duties," the daily quoted a federal information ministry statement as saying.
The only exemptions are goods free of duty under the former General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade or are of strategic importance for the national economy, it said.

Customs tariffs of one to five percent will be levied on raw materials and semi-finished goods that are not produced by the national industry, and from six to 12 percent on those produced in insufficient quantities.
A tax of 13-21 percent will be imposed on raw materials, semi-finished goods and spare parts produced in Yugoslavia in sufficient quantities.
A customs duty between 21 and 30 percent is proposed for equipment produced in Yugoslavia while a lower duty of one to 15 percent for equipment not produced in the country.
Import duty for consumer goods would be 31-40 percent.
The new customs tariffs should take effect on August 1.
The government has submitted the customs tariffs bill to the federal parliament for adoption at its next session which it proposed for June 26.

The government has also decided to introduce a special tax for the import of some agricutural and food products to protect domestic production. No details were given. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
